groups.title: Lab Totals and activities
groups.intro: The Lab Total, seasons in the lab, help, distractions and doing several things at once.

entries.title: Basic Laboratory Activities
entries.summary: Introduces the Lab Total, the sum used for most laboratory tasks, built from the Technique and Form relevant to the task; activities based on it require a laboratory.
quotes: YOUR BASIC LAB TOTAL IS: Technique + Form + Intelligence + Magic Theory + Aura Modifier

entries.title: Creating a Laboratory
entries.summary: A laboratory needs a protected room of at least 500 square feet and a ten-foot ceiling and a Magic Theory score of 3; the first season gives a basic laboratory with a Lab Total penalty and the second completes a standard one.
quotes: A character must have a Magic Theory score of at least 3 to set up a laboratory, and overall it takes two seasons of work.

entries.title: Arcane Studies
entries.summary: Points out that Art scores and Magic Theory can be raised in several ways, all described in the Experience and Advancement section.
quotes: Magi may increase their Art scores in several different ways.

entries.title: Vis Use
entries.summary: A magus can use only a limited amount of raw vis in laboratory work per season.
quotes: VIS LIMIT: Magic Theory x 2 pawns per season

entries.title: Multiple Laboratory Activities
entries.summary: Several easy lab activities of the same type, Technique and Form can be done in one season by summing their levels against the Lab Total, using the lowest total if they differ.
quotes: add up the levels of all activities performed and apply your Lab Total to the total of the levels
apply the lowest of the Lab Totals to the total of the levels

entries.title: Fixing Arcane Connections
entries.summary: An active Arcane Connection can be made permanent with a season of laboratory work and one pawn of Vim vis, without using a Lab Total.
quotes: may make it permanent by spending a season of laboratory work and one pawn of Vim vis

entries.title: Vis Transfer
entries.summary: Raw vis can be moved to another physical form in a laboratory in a day, up to the item's capacity from the Material and Size Table, without changing the Art it is attuned to.
quotes: This takes a day (from sunrise to sunrise), and can be done while the magus is engaged in another laboratory activity.

related.text: ArM5 p.255 Material and Size Table

entries.title: Distractions from Lab Work
entries.summary: Missing days from a lab season carries no penalty up to a limit, then reduces the Lab Total, and prevents lab work entirely if too many days are missed.
quotes: your Lab Total is penalized by 10 points, plus two points for every day over ten that you miss, up to a maximum penalty of 30 when you miss twenty days

groups.title: Inventing and learning spells
groups.intro: Inventing new spells, learning them from texts, and similar spells.

entries.title: Learning Spells from a Teacher
entries.summary: A season with a teaching magus lets a student learn spell levels up to the teacher's Lab Total (overall and per Technique and Form), with no spell above the student's own Lab Total.
quotes: MAXIMUM TOTAL LEVELS: Teacher's highest applicable Lab Total
MAXIMUM LEVELS IN ONE TECHNIQUE AND FORM: Teacher's Lab Total in that Technique and Form
HIGHEST LEVEL OF AN INDIVIDUAL SPELL: Student's Lab Total in the Technique and Form of the Spell

entries.title: Inventing Spells
entries.summary: How to invent a spell: set its effect and level, then accumulate a season's points equal to the amount by which the Lab Total (with a bonus for similar spells and requisites) exceeds the spell level until the level is reached; Lab Texts make this much faster.
quotes: You can only invent a spell if your Lab Total exceeds the spell's level.
For each point that your Lab Total exceeds the spell's level, you accumulate one point per season.

related.text: ArM5 p.303 Changing Ranges, Durations and Targets

entries.title: Example: Inventing Spells
entries.summary: Worked example of computing a Rego Vim Lab Total and how many seasons it takes to invent a level 20 ward versus a level 12 or 13 ward.
quotes: Tillitus's Lab Total of 25 exceeds the spell level, 20, by 5, so every season Tillitus gains 5 points towards the spell.

entries.title: Similar Spells
entries.summary: Knowing a similar spell adds its magnitude to the Lab Total for inventing or enchanting; only the highest applies, and similarity is defined by effect and parameters.
quotes: SIMILAR SPELL BONUS: Magnitude of highest-level similar spell known

groups.title: Enchanted items
groups.intro: Opening an item, invested devices, charged and lesser enchantments, and effects.

entries.title: Enchantments: Overview and Limits
entries.summary: Introduces enchanted devices (invested, lesser, charged items and longevity rituals), notes that enchanting transforms vis permanently, and bars Ritual-equivalent effects from items except those that are Rituals only because of level.
quotes: Effects matching those of Ritual spells may not be placed in any enchantment.

entries.title: Enchantment Summary
entries.summary: Step-by-step sidebar summarising how to choose an item type, open it, invest effects, and fill an invested item, including the per-season vis limit.
quotes: A magus cannot use more than 2 x Magic Theory pawns of vis in a single season.
Uses a number of pawns of Vim vis equal to the product of the material base and the size multiplier, from the Size and Material table.

entries.title: Invested Items
entries.summary: Invested items must be prepared first but can then hold multiple effects, up to the vis capacity used to open them; effects cannot be removed once instilled.
quotes: The total number of pawns of vis expended when instilling effects may not exceed the number of pawns of vis spent to prepare the item for enchantment.

entries.title: Lesser Enchantments
entries.summary: Cheaper unopened items that hold a single effect which must be instilled in one season; vis is spent per ten levels of the effect and the item's size/material still caps it.
quotes: his Lab Total must be at least twice the adjusted level of the effect.
Investing an effect in a lesser enchantment costs one pawn of appropriate vis for every ten levels or fraction of the effect

entries.title: Charged Items
entries.summary: Charged items cost no vis and are made in a single season, producing a number of single-use charges based on how far the Lab Total exceeds the effect level; charges can be split among identical objects.
quotes: For every 5 points, or fraction thereof, by which you exceed the level, you get one charge
If your Lab Total is less than the level of the effect you cannot create charged items of this kind.

entries.title: Preparation for Enchantment
entries.summary: Rules for spending a season and raw Vim vis to open an item, including enchanting part of an item, compound items (sum or highest), limits on components, and items larger than huge.
quotes: The multiplier increases by one for every factor of ten by which the item is larger than a huge item
A compound item of this sort may not contain more components than your Magic Theory score

entries.title: Instilling Effects
entries.summary: Introduces designing and instilling effects, which are built like spells but need not be known as spells and cost no extra design time.

entries.title: Designing the Effect
entries.summary: How to define an item effect from spell guidelines, track its base and modified level, choose a frequency and trigger, and optionally link triggers to other effects.
quotes: Enchanted device effects may have a level over 50, as long as there is no other reason for the spell to be a ritual

entries.title: Effect Frequency Table
entries.summary: Table of level modifiers added to an effect for uses per day, up to unlimited.
quotes: | Unlimited | +10 |

entries.title: Effect Modifications
entries.summary: Optional modifications to an item effect: Penetration, Concentration, restricted users, expiry (multiplying the excess), environmental, fast and linked triggers, each with its level cost.
quotes: For every level you add to the effect's level, that effect gets +2 Penetration.
This option adds +5 to the effect's level.
A linked trigger adds +3 to the level of the triggered effect.

entries.title: Instilling the Effect
entries.summary: The ritual of joining: compare your Lab Total, with requisite, shape/material, shared-art and similar-spell modifiers, to the modified effect level, accumulating points per season, and spend vis per ten levels of the effect.
quotes: For each effect already in the device that has a Technique and/or Form in common with the effect being invested, add +1 to your Lab Total.
you must also expend one pawn of raw vis of an Art matching either the Technique or Form of the effect being invested

entries.title: Constant Effect Devices
entries.summary: How to build an item with a truly continuous effect using Sun duration, a use frequency and an environmental trigger.

entries.title: Using Enchanted Devices
entries.summary: Default rules for using enchanted devices: zero Penetration, range measured from the device, wielder's Finesse for targeting, one trigger action per round and initiative timing.
quotes: Effects produced by enchanted devices have a Penetration of zero.
You use an enchanted device at an Initiative point equal to Qik + Stress Die.

entries.title: Investigating Enchantments
entries.summary: Procedure for learning the powers of someone else's enchanted item in the lab, rolling Intellego Vim from weakest to strongest power, with botch consequences and Waiting Spell warnings.
quotes: you spend a season, add a stress die to your Intellego Vim Lab Total, and compare the result to the level of the weakest power in the enchantment

entries.title: Effect Modification for Enchanted Items
entries.summary: New enchanting modification, Fast Trigger, which speeds an item effect's Initiative at a cost in effect level.
quotes: The effect gains a +3 Initiative modifier. This adds +5 to the level of the effect.

groups.title: Talismans
groups.intro: The magus's Talisman: opening, attunement and its bonuses.

entries.title: Talisman Attunement
entries.summary: Rules for attuning a self-prepared item as a talisman: only one at a time, treated as part of the magus, Arcane Connection, larger capacity opened gradually, Lab Total bonus when instilling, and shape-and-material attunements giving Casting Score bonuses.
quotes: The maximum number of pawns of Vim vis that may be used to prepare a talisman is equal to the sum of the magus's highest Technique and highest Form.
he gets a +5 bonus to his Lab Total

groups.title: Shape and Material bonuses
groups.intro: Bonuses from an item's shape and material.

entries.title: Shape and Material
entries.summary: Choosing an item's shape and material grants Lab Total bonuses from the Shape and Material Bonuses Table; bonuses stack but are capped by Magic Theory.
quotes: the highest bonus that you can receive to a single enchantment is equal to your Magic Theory

entries.title: Material and Size Tables
entries.summary: Tables giving the base points of each material and the multiplier by item size; their product is the pawns of Vim vis needed to open an item.

entries.title: Shape and Material Bonuses Table
entries.summary: Alphabetical table of shapes and materials with the Lab Total bonuses they give to matching enchantment effects, used for invested items, charged items and talisman attunements.
quotes: Triple the bonus for the type of wood (oak, ash, etc), but not for wood as such.
+4 control things at a distance

entries.title: Shape and Material Bonus Table Additions
entries.summary: New Shape and Material bonus entries for amber, human skull, lead, mirror, opal and rhodocrosite, listing the effect types each material supports.
quotes: Amber: +3 Controlling movement.

entries.title: Tremere Enchanting Materials (Amber, Rhodocrosite, Opal)
entries.summary: Identifies amber, rhodocrosite and opal as the typical materials for minor Tremere items, their classification (semiprecious or precious) for enchantment cost, and the effects each assists.
quotes: Amber and rhodocrosite are semiprecious gems for enchantment cost calculation; opal is precious.

related.text: Shape and Material Bonus Table Additions

entries.title: Shape & Material Bonuses: Tools
entries.summary: An expanded table of tools and the Shape and Material bonus each gives when enchanted, for use in lab totals and items of quality.
quotes: +3 reaping, +3 year-duration effects, +4 effects expressly causing death

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material bonuses

entries.title: Shape & Material Bonuses: Trees
entries.summary: An expanded table of tree woods and the Shape and Material bonus each gives to specific kinds of effect.
quotes: +6 strength, +6 Vim on hostile magic

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material bonuses

entries.title: Shape & Material Bonuses: Trees under Special Circumstances
entries.summary: Bonuses for wood that is dead, struck by lightning or a twisted tree in a field, for use alongside the tree table.
quotes: +3 affect living wood, +4 affect dead wood

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material bonuses

entries.title: Shape & Material Bonuses: Minerals
entries.summary: An expanded table of stones, metals and other minerals and the Shape and Material bonus each gives to specific kinds of effect.
quotes: +5 dragons, +4 wealth, +4 language, +3 long life

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material bonuses

entries.title: Shape and Material Bonuses for Herbs of Virtue
entries.summary: List of the shape and material bonuses that each example Herb of Virtue provides to enchantments.
quotes: +7 divination

entries.title: Shape and Material Bonuses for Objects of Virtue
entries.summary: List of the shape and material bonuses that each example Formed Stone or Object of Virtue provides to enchantments.
quotes: +2 arthritis

entries.title: Enriching a Thing of Virtue
entries.summary: Procedure for Enriching Herbs and Objects of Virtue with a season of magical operation to grant a Virtue to the wearer, including the Magic Lore roll to learn the method, the Enrichment Total, the Virtues conferred, drawbacks and Warping.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 9
Enrichment Total: Intelligence + Magic Lore + aura

related.text: ArM5 p.184 Penetration of Supernatural Abilities

entries.title: Hedge Magicians and Enriched Things of Virtue
entries.summary: How ungifted hedge magicians use Enriched Things of Virtue to gain minor powers at the cost of accumulating Warping.
quotes: The mechanics of Enriching a Thing of Virtue allow an unGifted character to acquire minor magical powers.

entries.title: Hermetic Magi and Enriched Things of Virtue
entries.summary: Why magi rarely benefit from Enriched Things of Virtue and how one can be built into an invested item or talisman.
quotes: An invested item made from an Enriched Thing of Virtue can only be made into a talisman if the magus Enriched the item himself.

entries.title: Objects of Virtue
entries.summary: Objects of Virtue derive their Virtues from the same Shape and Material Bonuses magi use, and any vis-bearing item with such a bonus to an Art can be Enriched to confer Puissant Art.
quotes: can be Enriched to confer Puissant Art

groups.title: Lab texts
groups.intro: Writing, reading and translating laboratory texts.

entries.title: Laboratory Texts
entries.summary: Introduces Laboratory Texts: one text is produced for every effect a magus creates, and they greatly speed reproduction of spells and enchantments.

entries.title: Using Laboratory Texts
entries.summary: Working from a Lab Text lets a magus reproduce an effect in a season if the Lab Total reaches its level, with limits on changes, talismans and experimentation, plus rules for rewriting and copying texts for others.
quotes: WRITING LABORATORY TEXTS: Latin x 20 levels per season
COPYING LABORATORY TEXTS: Profession: Scribe x 60 levels per season
A magus who has a Laboratory Text for a particular effect may reproduce it in a single season if his Lab Total equals or exceeds the level of the effect.

entries.title: Casting Tablets
entries.summary: Casting Tablets let a magus cast a spell he has not learned, using a fixed set of parameters from the author, with an inflexible casting total and a table of Fatigue loss and Warping depending on the margin.
quotes: CASTING TOTAL: Stamina + Form + Technique + Aura + stress die (modified by Virtues, Flaws and requisites)
0 or more | Spell cast, lose one Fatigue level.

entries.title: Translating Laboratory Texts
entries.summary: Decoding another magus's shorthand takes seasons of study accumulating Lab Total points up to the effect's level; once decoded, his other texts up to that level can be rewritten.
quotes: you accumulate a number of points equal to your Lab Total in the appropriate Technique and Form

groups.title: Familiars
groups.intro: Finding and binding a familiar, its cords and what it can do.

entries.title: Familiars
entries.summary: Overview of familiars: magically bonded animals that become a magus's closest companion while keeping their own will.

entries.title: Finding and Befriending an Animal
entries.summary: The first step to a familiar is finding a magical animal (left to the storyguide) and genuinely befriending it without coercion.

entries.title: Enchanting the Familiar
entries.summary: Enchanting a familiar differs from ordinary enchantment because the bond changes both parties and the troupe decides how the magus is affected.

entries.title: Suggested Familiars by Art
entries.summary: List of animals suited to bonding with each Technique and Form.

entries.title: The Initial Bond
entries.summary: Lab Total, enchantment level (based on Magic Might and Size) and vis cost for binding a familiar in a single season, using Arts appropriate to the animal.
quotes: FAMILIAR BONDING LAB TOTAL: Any Technique + any Form + Intelligence + Magic Theory + Aura Modifier
FAMILIAR BONDING LEVEL: Familiar's Magic Might + 25 + (5 x Size)
FAMILIAR BONDING COST: 1 pawn of vis per five levels or fraction of the binding Lab Total. Vis must match Technique or Form

entries.title: The Three Cords
entries.summary: The Lab Total is divided to buy golden, silver and bronze cord scores that give botch-dice reduction, mental protection and bonuses to Personality rolls, and physical resilience bonuses; cords can be strengthened later.
quotes: A cord strength of 0 costs nothing, a strength of +1 requires 5 points, a score of +2 requires 15 points, a score of +3 requires 30 points, a score of +4 requires 50 points, and a score of +5 (the maximum) requires 75 points
The total cost of the cords you buy cannot exceed the magus's Lab Total.

entries.title: The Bound Familiar
entries.summary: Effects of the completed bond: True Friend Virtue and Loyalty trait, no natural death while the magus lives, human-level intelligence, shared Arcane Connection and Magic Resistance rules.
quotes: The familiar uses the better of its Magic Resistance or the magus's Form resistance to resist spells, but this resistance does not stack with a Parma Magica.

entries.title: Empowering the Bond
entries.summary: Investing powers in the familiar bond follows invested-device rules with four exceptions: unlimited powers, matching-Art bonuses to the Lab Total instead of existing effects, targets limited to the pair, and no Verditius bonus; such powers avoid Warping.
quotes: she gets +5 if the effect matches either the Technique or Form used to bind the familiar, and +10 if it matches both
the power does not cause Warping (page 389) as a constant mystical effect

entries.title: The Familiar in Play
entries.summary: Describes how a familiar learns and ages alongside the magus, the consequences when one dies, and that a magus may have only one familiar.
quotes: You can only have one familiar at a time.

entries.title: Example Powers
entries.summary: Worked examples of effects commonly invested in familiar bonds (speech, mental communication, shapechanging, shared senses, location, aura of fire, claws) with their level breakdowns.

groups.title: Longevity Rituals
groups.intro: Making a Longevity Ritual for oneself or others.

entries.title: Longevity Rituals
entries.summary: A season-long lab ritual that reduces aging rolls, costs vis by the subject's age, makes the subject sterile, and lapses at an aging crisis; it can be improved with extra vis and performed for others, including non-magi at a reduced benefit.
quotes: LONGEVITY RITUAL: +1 bonus for every five points or fraction of Creo Corpus Lab Total
LONGEVITY RITUAL VIS COST: 1 pawn for every five years of age (rounded up)
For each additional pawn you add to the ritual, add 1 to your Lab Total.

entries.title: Longevity Rituals for Mundanes
entries.summary: Applies the Longevity Ritual rules to people without supernatural abilities, giving the requirements and costs, and lists the drawbacks of Warping, overstaying one's welcome and loss of fertility.
quotes: the magus needs a Creo Corpus Lab Total of at least 30
the beneficiary of the Longevity Ritual gains one Warping Point per year

entries.title: Vis Extraction
entries.summary: A season spent in a Magical aura extracting raw vis yields Vim vis based on the Creo Vim Lab Total.
quotes: VIS EXTRACTION: One tenth (round up) of Creo Vim Lab Total pawns of Vim vis

groups.title: Assistants and apprentices
groups.intro: Lab assistants, apprentices, and training them.

entries.title: Help in the Laboratory
entries.summary: Gifted helpers with Magic Theory add their Intelligence plus Magic Theory (and relevant Virtues/Flaws) to the primary researcher's Lab Total, with a limit on the number of assistants set by Leadership and social implications for helpers.
quotes: you add the helper's Intelligence + Magic Theory to your Lab Total for the season
is limited to his Leadership score (though he can always have at least one)

entries.title: Finding Your Apprentice
entries.summary: Apprentices must have The Gift and may be found by story or by a seasonal stress roll; also notes the usual age range and how apprentices are obtained.
quotes: For every season you spend searching for a potential apprentice, make a stress die and add your Perception. If the result is 9+, you find one.

entries.title: Training Your Apprentice
entries.summary: Rules and Order law for teaching an apprentice: claims begin when the Arts are opened, at least one teaching season a year, Parma Magica sharing to counter The Gift, and ownership and transfer rules.
quotes: A magus must personally teach the apprentice for at least one season per year over the course of the apprenticeship

entries.title: Opening the Arts
entries.summary: The teaching season in which an apprentice receives a score of 0 in every Art; low Art scores in the master cause Deficiencies and existing Supernatural Abilities require an Intellego Vim Lab Total to preserve or convert.
quotes: If you have a score of less than five in any Art when you open them, your apprentice automatically has a Deficiency
you can only open the Arts if your Intellego Vim Lab Total equals or exceeds five times the apprentice's score in the relevant Ability

entries.title: Teaching Hermetic Virtues
entries.summary: A parens can teach a Hermetic Virtue he possesses to a Gifted apprentice in a season by generating a Teaching Source Quality against a target level, which rises with the student's existing Hermetic Virtues and can be eased by including a Hermetic Flaw.
quotes: TEACHING SOURCE QUALITY: Communication + Teaching + 3 + bonus
TEACHING A MINOR HERMETIC VIRTUE: Target level is 15
TEACHING A MAJOR HERMETIC VIRTUE: Target Level is 21
Including a Minor Hermetic Flaw adds a +3 bonus. Including a Major Hermetic Flaw adds a +9 bonus.

entries.title: Acquiring House Virtues
entries.summary: How an apprentice gains the free Minor House Virtue: ten seasons of one-to-one interaction with the parens for most Houses, a package for Ex Miscellanea, or an Initiation into the Outer Mystery for Mystery Cult Houses.
quotes: ACQUIRING THE MINOR HERMETIC HOUSE VIRTUE: Requires 10 Seasons of one-to-one Interaction with Parens

entries.title: Gaining Hermetic Flaws
entries.summary: Explains how Hermetic Flaws gained after character generation take effect immediately and are permanent, typically gained from learning Virtues, uncontrolled Twilight or opening the Arts with a Deficiency.

entries.title: Fleshing Out Your Apprentice
entries.summary: An apprentice adds Intelligence plus Magic Theory to Lab Totals; to play one as a full character, create a young character with The Gift whose Arts the magus can open.

entries.title: The End of Apprenticeship
entries.summary: Apprenticeship ends with a gauntlet set by the parens after the usual term; after repeated failures the Quaesitores set the gauntlets.
quotes: If an apprentice fails three gauntlets, the Quaesitores set the fourth and subsequent gauntlets

entries.title: Opening the Arts in house Ex Miscellanea
entries.requires: House Ex Miscellanea tradition whose Major Virtue is an inborn Supernatural Virtue
entries.summary: Apprentices of certain Ex Miscellanea traditions need no minimum Intellego Vim Lab Total to keep the tradition's Major Virtue when the Arts are opened.

groups.title: Experimentation
groups.intro: Experimenting in the lab, the Extraordinary Results Chart and Arcane Discovery.

entries.title: Arcane Experimentation
entries.summary: Overview of experimenting when inventing spells, enchanting devices or familiars, or investigating enchantments, trading safety for the chance of exceeding normal capabilities.

entries.title: The Experimental Premise
entries.summary: Choosing to experiment at the start of a season adds a simple die to the Lab Total but requires a stress roll on the Extraordinary Results Chart each season; cannot be combined with working from a Lab Text.
quotes: add a simple die roll to your Lab Total

entries.title: Exceptional Risk
entries.summary: Optionally adding a risk modifier to the experiment die also adds it to every chart roll and gives extra botch dice equal to the modifier.
quotes: adding from +1 to +3 (your choice) to the die roll; this bonus is called your risk modifier
you get a number of extra botch dice on your rolls equal to your bonus

entries.title: Extraordinary Results
entries.summary: How to roll on and interpret the Extraordinary Results Chart (stress die plus risk modifier, botch dice including aura), and the option to recreate a flawed effect with a bonus of Magic Theory.
quotes: roll a stress die, adding your risk modifier (if any)
You also get one additional botch die for each point in the supernatural aura of the laboratory
you gain your Magic Theory score (your score at the time of your experiment) as a bonus to your Lab Total

entries.title: Inventing a Spell by Experimentation
entries.summary: The experimental die may let a spell be invented sooner or beyond normal capacity; if the total still falls short the spell is not invented but the chart is still rolled.

entries.title: Enchanted Items Created by Experimentation
entries.summary: When experimenting on an enchanted item, falling short loses the vis and still rolls on the chart, and a flawed effect still takes up capacity in the device.

entries.title: Experimenting on Longevity Rituals
entries.summary: Experimenting adds the simple die to a Longevity Ritual's Lab Total; a flawed ritual can be overridden by a second ritual in an extra season.

entries.title: Investigating an Enchanted Item by Experimentation
entries.summary: The simple die is added to every discovery roll when investigating an item, but chart results may damage the item unless its protections exceed the Lab Total.

entries.title: Extraordinary Results Chart
entries.summary: The chart and sub-tables for experiment outcomes: disaster by number of zeroes, side effects, no benefit, complete failure, special or story event, discovery rewards and modified effects.
quotes: Suffer the effect for the number you roll and for all lower numbers, unless explicitly told otherwise.
Roll a simple die and add your risk modifier.

entries.title: Enchanting a Familiar by Experimentation
entries.requires: A magus with a familiar being bound or empowered
entries.summary: Experimentation on a familiar bond adds the die as normal but risks tainting the bond.

groups.title: Original research
groups.intro: Breakthroughs and original research into new Hermetic theory.

entries.title: Arcane Discovery
entries.summary: Overview of how Hermetic magi can expand the Art through original research.

entries.title: The Breakthrough
entries.summary: Defines Minor, Major and Hermetic Breakthroughs and the approximate breakthrough points required for each, and how research may be experimental or based on non-Hermetic magic.
quotes: A Minor Breakthrough typically requires around 30 breakthrough points.
A Major Breakthrough typically requires around 45 breakthrough points.
A Hermetic Breakthrough typically requires around 60 breakthrough points.

entries.title: Experimentation (Arcane Discovery)
entries.summary: Original research uses experimentation but the risk modifier (limited by Magic Theory) adjusts the chart roll instead of the Lab Total, hoping for a Discovery result.
quotes: BREAKTHROUGH: Roll Discovery on the Extraordinary Results Chart during a season of Arcane Experimentation
RISK MODIFIER: +1 per 5 points of Magic Theory or fraction thereof, up to +3

entries.title: Stabilizing the Unknown
entries.summary: After a Discovery the experiment is repeated exactly to stabilize it, yielding breakthrough points equal to the magnitude but also Warping Points and possible Twilight.
quotes: SUCCESSFUL STABILIZATION SEASON: Magnitudes of Stabilized Discovery = Breakthrough Points
WARPING POINTS GAINED: The magnitude of the Stabilized Discovery

entries.title: Integration
entries.summary: Insight from non-Hermetic texts, relics or teachers, gained by a season's stress roll, lets a magus create a partially Hermetic effect and accumulate breakthrough points.
quotes: make a stress roll of Intelligence + Magic Theory against an Ease Factor of 18

entries.title: Creating the Effect
entries.summary: A specific insight dictates one exact effect that must be invented with experimentation, giving breakthrough points equal to its magnitude and a reproducible Lab Text.
quotes: the magus gains a number of breakthrough points equal to the magnitude of the effect

entries.title: After the Breakthrough
entries.summary: Describes what Minor, Major and Hermetic Breakthroughs allow once achieved, how Abilities and Virtues are taught or Initiated, and the effect of a second Major Breakthrough.

entries.title: Original Research
entries.summary: Introduction to original research, the process by which a magus tries to push the limits of Hermetic magic; notes that anyone can start at any time with no minimum Art or Ability.
quotes: There are no minimum Art or Ability requirements for undertaking original research

entries.title: Breakthroughs
entries.summary: Defines the three kinds of Breakthrough (Minor, Major, Hermetic), with examples of each, and advises discussing the target with the troupe first.
quotes: These achievements are called Breakthroughs and there are three types: Minor, Major, and Hermetic.

entries.title: Warping Points from Stabilizing a Discovery
entries.summary: Warping Points are gained whether stabilization succeeds or fails, and a failed stabilization may be retried in consecutive seasons.
quotes: Warping Points gained: the Magnitude of the Stabilized Discovery minus a simple die
You receive Warping Points whether you succeed or fail at stabilizing your discovery.

entries.title: Surpassing the Limits
entries.summary: When accumulated stabilized-discovery points reach a secret target set by the storyguide, a Breakthrough is achieved; gives a rule-of-thumb target by Breakthrough type and explains why the player should not know it.
quotes: A rough rule of thumb is 30 points are needed for a Minor Breakthrough, 45 for a Major and 60 for a true Hermetic Breakthrough.

entries.title: Multiple Laboratory Texts (Collaborative Research)
entries.summary: How a magus can add another magus's original-research Lab Texts to their own Breakthrough points by reading them for a season in a laboratory, without gaining Warping Points; the first researcher to reach the target makes the Breakthrough.
quotes: You accumulate points equal to your Lab Total in the Arts concerned.

entries.title: Breakthroughs in Play
entries.summary: How a completed Minor, Major or Hermetic Breakthrough is used and passed on to other magi (through a spell, personal teaching, tractatus, or as an Arcane Ability).
quotes: You do not have to subtract your total Hermetic Arts score from the Source Quality of the teaching source.

entries.title: Hermetic Integration
entries.summary: Explains how a further Breakthrough on a Major Breakthrough can fold its Virtue into ordinary Hermetic magic so that it no longer needs to be learned separately.

entries.title: Exempli Gratia: Original Research
entries.summary: A worked example following a magus through experiments, a Discovery roll with a risk modifier, and the stabilization season.

entries.title: Aristotelian and Platonic Magic Theory breakthroughs
entries.requires: Troupe decision that the breakthrough exists; research by a magus
entries.summary: Optional saga-level rules for researching Aristotelian or Platonic Magic Theory as a Hermetic breakthrough, which Arts must be used in the experiments, and what the finished breakthrough adds to a magus's totals. A tractatus lets others incorporate it as a minor breakthrough.
quotes: would allow a magus character to add his score in Artes Liberales to his Lab Totals and his formulaic spell casting totals

related.text: ArM5 Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.26 (original research)

entries.title: Arma Magica (Parma Folds)
entries.summary: Introduces the Arma Magica folds as Major Breakthroughs built on Parma Magica, and limits how many folds a magus can know and how many students can be taught a fold.
quotes: A magus may know a number of folds equal to his Parma Magica score.

entries.title: Parma Magica Folds
entries.summary: Rules for calculating magic resistance under the folds, and descriptions of the Ablativa, Absorbea, Condensa, Custodia, Repercussa and Restricta variants of Parma Magica with their effects, casting times and restrictions.
quotes: Double a magus's Parma Magica score when calculating magic resistance.
Double the Parma Magica score against the specified Form, but divide it by two (round up) against all others.
The magus adds twice his Parma Magica score to any Defense totals in combat.

entries.title: Parmulae
entries.summary: A lesser enchanted device giving its wearer fixed magic resistance for a limited time, with its construction cost, level of effect and limitations, plus a warning to discuss it with the troupe.
quotes: Parmulae: Lesser Enchanted Device that provides a magic resistance of 30. Total level of effect is 44.
Its base level of effect is Rego Vim 30.

entries.title: Figurine Magic
entries.summary: Procedure for crafting and enchanting short-lived wax or wood figurines for a single recipient, giving them a Minor Virtue or a Hermetic spell, with construction rolls, enchantment Ease Factors, and limits on which Virtues can be imbued.
quotes: Constructing a figurine takes a month for a wax figurine or two for a wood figurine.
Making a figure: Dexterity + Craft: Sculptor + Stress die
Enchanting a figure: Intelligence + Figurine Magic +Aura Modifier

entries.title: Realm-Aligned Spells
entries.requires: Saga option: Realm-Aligned Spell Minor Breakthrough
entries.summary: How to invent a spell flavored to the Magic, Faerie or Infernal realm so it is immune to that realm's normal interaction and rolls fewer botch dice, at the cost of a lower Lab Total during invention.
quotes: you reduce your Lab Total by limiting your Magic Theory Ability score to the level of your appropriate Realm Lore

entries.title: Realm-Aligned Spell Interaction Table
entries.requires: Saga option: Realm-Aligned Spell Minor Breakthrough
entries.summary: Table giving the aura bonus or penalty applied to a realm-aligned spell by aura type and spell flavor, replacing the normal Realm Interaction Table.

entries.title: Researching Binding Magic as a Breakthrough
entries.summary: Suggests that integrating faerie or hedge powers that enforce oaths could be a Minor or Major Hermetic Breakthrough, since Hermetic magic cannot directly enforce agreements.
quotes: Researching or integrating a particular faerie power might be a Minor Breakthrough, while allowing freedom to vary the parameters and create similar spells may be a Major Breakthrough.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.26

groups.title: Laboratory personalization
groups.intro: A laboratory's Size, Refinement, Virtues, Flaws and Specializations.

entries.title: Laboratory Personalization Rules
entries.summary: Introduces treating a laboratory as a character with eight Characteristics, Virtues and Flaws (Major, Minor or Free) and Specializations that add to Lab Totals.
quotes: Each laboratory is characterized by a set of eight Characteristics, with a standard (default) lab starting with scores of 0 in each.

entries.title: Laboratory Characteristics
entries.summary: Lists the eight lab Characteristics and the three-step procedure for determining a non-standard lab's scores from Size, Refinement and its Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: Size, Refinement, General Quality, Upkeep, Safety, Warping, Health, Aesthetics
Set the Safety to be equal to the Refinement.

entries.title: Lab Size
entries.summary: Size sets floor space and the Virtue points a lab can hold; occupied Size reduces Safety and surplus Size calls for the Empty Flaw; includes the table of Size against square feet.
quotes: each point of Size adds to the maximum permitted number of Virtue points minus Flaw points
for every full two points by which the Size exceeds the occupied Size, you should take the Empty Flaw
for each additional 500 square feet beyond 1500, add a further +1 to Size

entries.title: Size and Refinement Summary
entries.summary: Quick formulas for the limit on Virtue minus Flaw points, occupied Size and base Safety.
quotes: LIMIT OF VIRTUE POINTS MINUS FLAW POINTS: Size + Refinement
BASE SAFETY OF LAB: Refinement

entries.title: Lab Refinement
entries.summary: Refinement adds to the Virtue space and Safety; a fresh lab starts at 0 and each point takes a season of work, requiring Magic Theory three above the target, with a roll to gain Highly Organized or Spotless or to spot or gain Hidden Defect.
quotes: need a Magic Theory equal to at least the desired Refinement score, plus 3
If this meets an Ease Factor of 12, Highly Organized is gained.

entries.title: Lab General Quality
entries.summary: General Quality is a flat bonus or penalty to every Lab Total, excluding teaching and scribing of texts.
quotes: General Quality adds to all Lab Totals.

entries.title: Lab Upkeep
entries.summary: Upkeep sets the build and yearly maintenance cost of the lab; unaffordable upkeep leads to gaining Flaws, and raising Upkeep costs the difference in build cost.
quotes: A lab with an Upkeep of 0 costs 5 pounds to build and 1 pound per typical year of use to maintain.

entries.title: Lab Safety
entries.summary: Safety subtracts from the botch dice on lab activities, and an unsafe lab requires a seasonal simple-die check for a lab accident even for normally safe work.
quotes: The Safety score subtracts its value from the number of botch dice on all lab activities.

entries.title: Laboratory Specializations
entries.summary: Specializations add to Lab Totals for particular activities or Arts; a lab can hold a limited number, and the activity Specializations (experimentation, familiar, items, longevity, spells, teaching, texts, vis extraction) are defined here.
quotes: A lab can have at most two activity Specializations, plus four Art Specializations (at most two of which can be Techniques).

entries.title: Laboratory Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Lab Virtues and Flaws are balanced so that Virtue points minus Flaw points cannot exceed Size plus Refinement; some can be taken multiple times.
quotes: the number of points spent on Virtues, minus the number of points spent on Flaws, cannot exceed the Size + Refinement of the lab

entries.title: Adding and Removing Lab Virtues
entries.summary: Adding a lab Virtue needs free space and takes seasons of work by someone with sufficient Magic Theory; removal is only sometimes possible.
quotes: it takes one season of work to gain a Minor Virtue, and two seasons to gain a Major Virtue

entries.title: Adding and Removing Lab Flaws
entries.summary: Lab Flaws take effect immediately and free up space; removing them needs free points and takes seasons depending on size.
quotes: removing a Minor Flaw also takes one season, and removing a Major Flaw takes two seasons

entries.title: Laboratory Personalization (introduction)
entries.summary: Introduces the options for personalizing and specializing a laboratory, which add detail to the lab activities already covered in the core rules.

entries.title: The Standard Hermetic Laboratory
entries.summary: Defines the standard laboratory by size, outfitting cost and setup time, and says any requirement can be violated at the price of Flaws; a rushed or unskilled setup leaves the lab with a penalty or negative Refinement.
quotes: The required outfittings cost five Mythic Pounds to procure.
It takes someone with a Magic Theory of three or more two seasons of work to set up the lab.
albeit with the Basic Flaw (see below), giving a –3 penalty to all Lab Totals.

entries.title: Life in the Laboratory (Standard Routine)
entries.summary: The standard lab routine of hours per day and days per week, how many work days can be missed in a season without penalty, and the penalty for being away from the lab too long.
quotes: The standard lab routine assumes that a magus works in the lab for ten hours a day, six days a week.
Up to ten work days can be missed in a season (in any order) without penalty, provided that the lost time is made up by working on rest days.

entries.title: Lab Warping
entries.summary: A lab with positive Warping may warp each season's product, using the chart for side effects or modified effects, and carries matching Personality Traits.
quotes: If the result is less than or equal to the Warping score, then the product of that season's work (be it an item, spell, or something else) suffers Warping.

entries.title: Lab Health
entries.summary: Health adds to Wound Recovery rolls for inhabitants and half of it adds to the Living Conditions modifier for aging.
quotes: The Health score adds to any Wound Recovery rolls for inhabitants of the lab.

entries.title: Lab Aesthetics
entries.summary: Aesthetics gives its owner experience points in an appropriate Reputation based on the lab's impressiveness.
quotes: For every point of Aesthetics, either positive or negative, the owner gains five experience points in an appropriate Reputation.

entries.title: Build Point Cost for Starting Laboratories
entries.summary: Build Point costs for labs under Customized Covenant Creation, including costs for extra labs, Size, and Minor and Major Virtues, with guidance for different covenant ages.
quotes: Extra (spare) labs cost 50 Build Points each.
Each Minor Virtue costs 10 Build Points and each Major Virtue costs 20 Build Points.

alsoIn.title: Build Point Cost for Starting Laboratories

entries.title: Structure Virtues and Flaws (Laboratory)
entries.summary: Lab Virtues and Flaws arising from the lab's physical structure and location (features, environment, stores, gallery, deformities, low ceilings, focus), with their effects on Characteristics and Specializations.
quotes: Greater Feature
Lesser Focus

entries.title: Outfittings Virtues and Flaws (Laboratory)
entries.summary: Lab Virtues and Flaws from equipment and occupants (expansions, living quarters, assistants, servants, organization, missing equipment or ingredients, damage, elementary labs).
quotes: Highly Organized
Missing Ingredients

entries.title: Supernatural Virtues and Flaws (Laboratory)
entries.summary: Lab Virtues and Flaws from supernatural sources (guardians, vis sources, enchantments, magic items, regios, hauntings, illusions).
quotes: Greater Guardian
Magic Item

entries.title: Laboratory Features
entries.summary: Lesser and Greater Features provide one or three points among listed Specializations; a lab can focus on one Feature, and the section lists example Features with their allowed Specializations.
quotes: The former provides three points on Specialization(s), the latter one point.

entries.title: Magic Items for Laboratories
entries.summary: Magic items or enchantments on a lab can grant lab Virtues and Flaws, or add to Characteristics or Specializations in proportion to effect level.
quotes: Every ten levels may grant one point in a Specialization, or every 20 levels may improve a Characteristic by one point.

entries.title: The Principles of Labwork
entries.summary: Seven principles behind a functioning laboratory (experimentation, documentation, comfort, sympathy, quality, extent, focus), used as a guide to what makes a lab effective and how it can be personalized.
quotes: The functioning of a Hermetic laboratory can be illustrated by listing seven main principles or factors that play a key role.

entries.title: Non-Standard Laboratory Routines
entries.summary: Optional seasonal routines (Early Riser, Nocturnal, Addled, Overtime, Double Overtime, Triple Overtime) that boost the Lab Total at the cost of Fatigue, Living Conditions, Aging rolls, Warping Points, extra botch dice and, for Addled, a recovery roll; working fewer hours reduces the totals.
quotes: for each hour fewer, she simply loses 10% of her Lab Total or Advancement Total for the season.
gain +1 to the Lab Total for the season.
gain +2 to the Lab Total for the season.
she gains +9 to the Lab Total for the season.

entries.title: Second Laboratories
entries.summary: Sidebar on why few magi keep a second lab, noting that the Peripheral Code allows only one sanctum and that a lab must occupy a single chamber.
quotes: the Peripheral Code only allows a magus to maintain one sanctum

entries.title: Taking Over a Laboratory
entries.summary: Sidebar on moving into a lab previously owned by someone else: when the new owner can start work at once, and when a season of rearrangement is needed, including the secret Perception + Magic Theory roll that may leave the Predecessor or Hidden Defect Flaw.
quotes: Finally, the storyguide should secretly make a Perception + Magic Theory roll against an Ease Factor of three times the lab's original Refinement for the maga.
the resulting Refinement score of the lab is equal to its old Refinement, or the new owner's Magic Theory – 3, whichever is lower.

entries.title: Moving a Laboratory
entries.summary: Sidebar giving the procedure and cost of relocating a lab: a season to pack it, transport that costs as much as years of maintenance, and two seasons to reassemble it.
quotes: the transport counts (and costs) as two entire years of maintenance.
This takes two seasons, since it is basically the same as building a lab from scratch

entries.title: Common Laboratory Items
entries.summary: Guidance on which lab Virtues, Characteristics or Specializations common enchanted items (lights, heaters, tools, decorations, purifying containers) can reasonably grant.
quotes: Items that provide light may negate the need for candles and lanterns, and grant the Magical Lighting Virtue.

entries.title: Spells for Laboratories
entries.summary: Rules for using spells to improve a lab: Ritual spells give permanent effects, regularly used non-Ritual spells cost Warping or Safety, and a magus may not boost a Lab Total with spells of the same Arts as the Lab Total.
quotes: As a rule of thumb, for each such spell that is employed regularly, either add one to the lab's Warping Characteristic or subtract one from its Safety.
A magus can never gain a bonus to Lab Totals (either from General Quality or a Specialization) by casting spells that use the same Arts as those in the Lab Total.

groups.title: Experimental philosophy
groups.intro: The mundane scholar's laboratory: ligatures, formulae and alchemical reagents.

entries.title: Experimental Philosophy
entries.summary: Introduces experimental philosophy: its products are natural rather than supernatural, so they ignore auras, Magic Resistance and Warping, cannot be enhanced by vis or spells, and require no Gift.
quotes: unaffected by supernatural auras and do not need to penetrate Magic Resistance to have an effect
vis has no use to the philosopher

entries.title: Natural Principles
entries.summary: Describes the natural principles behind philosophical work and Shape and Material bonuses: prime qualities, contagion, affinity, similarity, hidden virtues and astrology.
quotes: Magi know the products of this principle as Arcane Connections
Similarity imbues many objects with their Shape and Material bonuses.

entries.title: Ligatures
entries.summary: A ligature is a one-use charm built from an Arcane or Sympathetic Connection and natural principles that adds a bonus to a single roll in a limited time window. It is made by a character with an academic Ability and rolled for at creation.
quotes: Int + Academic Ability + stress die
If the result is nine or greater, then some benefit is gained
An individual can only have one ligature granting him a bonus at any time (even botched ones)

related.text: The Practice of the Apothecary, Pharmacy

entries.title: Formulae
entries.summary: Introduces formulae, recipes for astrological inceptions, alchemical reagents and pharmaceutical theriacs, which are first researched and then concocted in a laboratory without needing the Gift or supernatural aid.
quotes: A formula is a recipe, similar to a Laboratory Text, which describes how to make one of three products
The Gift is not required to concoct a formula

entries.title: Ligature Bonus Table
entries.summary: Table converting the total rolled when creating a ligature into the bonus it grants.
quotes: +3 (max)

entries.title: Example Ligatures
entries.summary: Lists, by Academic Ability and sub-field, the kinds of action a ligature can assist, and notes that ligatures cannot help craft ligatures and that medical ligatures cannot affect recovery rolls.
quotes: A ligature cannot assist with the crafting of a ligature.
Medical ligatures cannot affect either Wound Recovery rolls or Disease Recovery rolls.

entries.title: Researching Formulae
entries.summary: A formula is learned by accumulating experience points from study or by spending a season of Practice, after which it can be used to create products. A philosopher may learn a formula he cannot yet create.
quotes: Once the formula has accumulated 5 experience points, it has been learned
the philosopher earns 5 experience points towards the formula

entries.title: Converting Characters
entries.summary: Lets an existing character trade experience in an Academic Ability for formulae of the matching type.
quotes: Every 5 experience points removed from a character's total grants one formula of the appropriate type.

entries.title: Concocting a Formula
entries.summary: A philosopher needs a laboratory of minimum size and ceiling height, similar to a Hermetic laboratory but usable in any aura.
quotes: The philosopher requires at least 500 square feet of floor area and a ceiling at least ten feet high.

entries.title: The Laboratories of Philosophers
entries.summary: Explains that magi and philosophers must re-arrange a lab to share it, how to treat a philosopher's workspace under the Covenants upkeep rules, and which laboratory features carry over to a philosopher.
quotes: treat the philosopher's working space as an extra laboratory with an Upkeep score of –3
a philosopher cannot receive any benefit from a Supernatural Virtue or Flaw, but he can still suffer the downsides

entries.title: The Lab Total
entries.summary: Defines a philosopher's Lab Total for all formulae, the sources of Philosophic Bonuses (Shape and Material, Risk Modifiers from experimentation, and laboratory bonuses), and how seasons accumulate points toward completing a formula.
quotes: Lab Total: Intelligence + Academic Ability + Philosophic Bonuses
The Philosophic Bonuses that add to the Lab Total can never exceed the Ability used in the formula
for every season of working on the effect, the philosopher accumulates 1 point for each point by which his Lab Total exceeds the formula's level

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material Bonuses

entries.title: Laboratory Texts (Formulae)
entries.summary: The first time a formula is completed, a Laboratory Text is made that lets the philosopher make multiple doses on later occasions. The text can be copied for others like a Hermetic text, but the reader must also learn the formula.
quotes: (Lab Total) / 5 (round up)
cost a number of covenant Build Points equal to half their level

entries.title: Astrological Inceptions
entries.summary: An inception is an astrological chart that answers a question about a target once the target's nativity horoscope is calculated. It cannot simply be copied, only re-created from its Laboratory Text.
quotes: Int + Artes Liberales + die roll, against Ease Factor 9
it takes one minute per level of the inception to complete the calculation and reveal the answers sought
astrological inceptions cannot be simply copied

entries.title: When's My Birthday?
entries.summary: Advice on whether characters know their birth date and place, and how imprecise information reduces the Detail an inception can reveal. Also notes Hermetic attitudes to inceptions.
quotes: the inception should be treated as one Detail category less

entries.title: Inception Guidelines
entries.summary: Gives the Detail parameter for inceptions (Binary, Basic, Brief, Thorough), the magnitude adjustments for asking about the past or future, and base levels for the information gained.
quotes: A one-word answer between two choices (+0 magnitudes)
Reveals all relevant information associated with the target of the inception (+3 magnitudes)
Queries about the present add no magnitudes.

entries.title: Guidance on Using Astrological Inceptions
entries.summary: Storyguide advice on keeping inceptions from derailing stories: horoscopes show characteristics not motives, answer only indirect questions, do not fix destiny, and never give absolute answers.
quotes: The stars hold the answers to indirect questions only

entries.title: Replicating Formulae with Hermetic Magic
entries.summary: Describes how Rego Craft or Creo magic can assemble a reagent or theriac in an instant, the requisites to use, and the Finesse roll needed. Astrological inceptions cannot be duplicated this way.
quotes: The Ease Factor of this Finesse roll is the level of the formula + 9
A different spell is required for duplicating each formula.
Craft magic cannot duplicate astrological inceptions

entries.title: Alchemical Reagents
entries.summary: Reagents are natural substances made in a laboratory that alter the prime qualities of matter but cannot create matter or change the base substance. Concocting one draws on an apothecary's stores.
quotes: they have the equivalent of a Momentary Duration
Alchemy cannot transform the base substance into another sort, nor can it cause an increase or decrease in the amount of matter
1 Labor Point per 5 points (or fraction) of the level

related.text: Chapter Three: Philosophiae, Change in Quality

entries.title: Reagent Guidelines
entries.summary: Defines the Alteration parameter for reagents (Slight, Minor, Substantial, Major) with its effect on damage and magnitudes, the volume of matter affected and how size scales, and base levels for changing or purifying simple and complex matter.
quotes: A Reagent can affect one cubic pace of simple matter, or else fifty cubic inches of complex matter.
Each additional magnitude multiplies the base amount of matter by ten.
Enhance or diminish primary quality of simple matter

related.text: ArM5 p.97 Material and Size table

entries.title: Volume Conversion Guide
entries.summary: Converts the volume steps used for reagent size into familiar quantities, spheres, base Individuals and Material and Size categories.
quotes: Each increase in size on this chart indicates approximately a ten-fold increase in volume.

related.text: ArM5 p.97 Material and Size table

entries.title: Alchemical Purification's Shape & Material Bonuses
entries.summary: Alchemical purification can strengthen material-based Shape and Material bonuses, by an amount set by the Alteration level, and a short list of new bonuses is given that philosophers and magi can use.
quotes: A Minor Alteration can add a +1 to the bonus, a Substantial Alteration adds +2, and a Major Alteration adds +3.

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material Bonuses

entries.title: Pharmaceutical Theriacs
entries.summary: Theriacs are medicinal formulae learned as part of Medicine, made from an apothecary's ingredients, that can cure or cause wounds and disease effects.
quotes: Each Theriac costs an apothecary's business 1 Labor Point per 5 points (or fraction) of the level

entries.title: Theriac Guidelines
entries.summary: Defines the Potency parameter for theriacs (Weak to Mighty) and which wounds, diseases or Fatigue levels each can affect, plus base levels for Recovery roll bonuses, pain relief, poison reduction and causing wounds.
quotes: Affect a Light Wound, a Minor Disease, or Weary Fatigue level (+1 magnitude)
Grant a +3 to the patient's next Wound Recovery roll.
Different formulae are needed to affect Wound Recovery and Disease Recovery rolls.
